moments.body: You wrote it yourself: 'Yesterday was like a perfect day in Tokyo.' Michelin-star dinner, matcha, Golden Gai cocktails in bars the size of a wardrobe, Shibuya crossing at full tidal-wave scale, an arcade, an onsen, and a sake tasting where you ended up chatting with a high-ranking member of the Japanese air defense. Golden Gai's 200+ tiny bars tucked into six narrow alleys are one of Tokyo's most intimate experiences — the kind of place you can only find if someone takes you there.
moments.title: Perfect Day in Tokyo

moments.body: Tennis with Dave, a run, weights, sobriety held, the poolside cabana booked, meaningful Gremly progress — all in one day, in Bora Bora, after a long sleep that left you 'very very refreshed.' The lagoon at Bora Bora is one of the few places on earth where the water is genuinely turquoise rather than photographically enhanced. You were working and resting and competing and building — all at once. Days like this are worth remembering precisely.

spotlight.title: You held the streak through a sake tasting
spotlight.takeaway: You participated fully in a cultural ritual — met locals, made memories — without abandoning a 3-month commitment. That's a meaningful distinction: sobriety as identity rather than avoidance.
spotlight.evidence_trail: Feb 28: You completed 'Organize Sake Tasting in Japan' — you planned and attended a cultural tasting event. Mar 2 journal: 'a sake tasting where we met some funny locals' — you were present, social, meeting people. Then Mar 8 journal: 'very happy to have managed to fit in tennis, a quick run and some weights whilst also avoiding alcohol' — you called out sobriety as a win on a separate day, suggesting the tasting didn't break the streak. Habit data shows 6/21 (29%) completions across the full measurement period, consistent with selective tracking rather than collapse.

research_context.body: Social drinking cues are among the strongest behavioral triggers because they combine environmental context, peer modeling, and emotional reward simultaneously. Maintaining a commitment in exactly the setting designed to dissolve it — a sake tasting with new friends — requires what researchers call 'implementation intentions': pre-decided responses to anticipated temptation. The fact that you planned the tasting yourself suggests the decision was made consciously, not reactively.

cards.body: March opened with a launch and a flight to Tokyo on the same weekend — the kind of week that would break most people's routines. Instead, you used the honeymoon as a field test: for your fitness discipline, your sobriety commitment, your app's core feature, and your relationship. The thread that moved most quietly but most meaningfully was the one with Dave — from 'perfect day in Tokyo' to 'loved spending time on the floaties', the month built a record of presence that no productivity metric captures.
cards.headline: The month you shipped, honeymooned, and kept building — all at once

thread_arcs.arc: Launched TestFlight to friends and family on Feb 26, then iterated on the Daily Context Object across the first two weeks of March — from a beach in Bora Bora.
Arrived with shabu shabu and an onsen on day one; concluded March 6 with 'It was incredible and I cannot wait to be back' — a full arc from anticipation to gratitude.
Moved from shared excitement in Tokyo through a conscious mid-Bora Bora recalibration — 'I need to step back sometimes and just enjoy him' — to floaties and sunburn and sustained joy.
Exceeded weekly targets every week of the month, running in Tokyo, Bora Bora, and heading into Hawaii with the half marathon 14 days away.
Navigated a sake tasting in Japan and multiple social settings without breaking a commitment that started January 1 — now approaching the 10-week mark.
